decision: The repair is reported complete at no charge, but three closure checks are outstanding, so the ticket stays open on hold rather than being closed. Landlord authority for the instruction is already on file (event-006, the landlord's own "Yes please!", system-confirmed at event-007), and no spend decision arises because the contractor has confirmed the work is free of charge under the guarantee on the tap he fitted in February (event-050, consistent with event-025 and the agency's own "completed without payment" entry at event-052). Within my mandate I have: asked the tenant to confirm the shower and tap now work, including the extra symptom she reported to the contractor on 14 October (event-030); chased Keystone Services for the photographs the landlord has twice asked for (event-043, event-045) with a reply-by of 12:00 on 10 November 2026; reported the outcome and the nil cost to the landlord and told him we will seek his sign-off once photos and tenant confirmation are in; logged the file note and placed the case on hold. I did not close the request: documents, landlord confirmation and tenant verification are still pending, and a closure with those open would be premature. I did not decide liability for the faulty tap or accept the contractor's "no charge" as a final financial position for the landlord to sign — the landlord confirms that (RTE-LANDLORD, PRO-TENANT-LIABILITY).
